subject: Gatecheck passport: liveness + traffic priming playbook
messages:
From: Eric Lowry <eric.lowry@acmecloud.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acmecloud.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gatecheck request — final week before VPC cutover

Camila / team,

Thank you for the updated timeline. We're aiming for a controlled cutover Thu 10 Jun (UTC) to move traffic from the old inference cluster to the Redwood private deployment inside our VPC. Before we schedule the ops window we need to validate a short set of items so our security and SRE teams can sign the gate:

- Liveness & readiness probes (commands and expected returns)
- KV-cache priming plan and ETA to reach steady hit rates
- Traffic priming/traffic-shift playbook for staged roll (10% -> 100%)
- Observability hooks (span tags, per-model latency metrics, token counters)

I've attached a short MOP with our constraints and the three compliance checks we require. Can you confirm the exact probe endpoints and a short acceptance test we can run from our side? Also please include any non-obvious failure modes (e.g., cache poisoning, cold-start amplification) we should watch for.

Eric
SRE, Acme Cloud

Attachments: cutover_mop_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 128KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Lowry <eric.lowry@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gatecheck request — final week before VPC cutover

Eric — thanks for the note and the MOP. Summary and attachments below. High level: we can meet all four checks; below is the quick acceptance test you can run from your side and the staged rollout cadence we recommend.

Quick acceptance tests (from your SRE jumpbox):
1) Liveness: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://internal-api.redwood/acme/v1/health/liveness -> 200 expected 
2) Readiness: curl -s https://internal-api.redwood/acme/v1/health/ready -> JSON {"ready":true, "kv_state":"warm"}
3) KV cache sample: curl -s https://internal-api.redwood/acme/v1/metrics/kv_hit_rate | grep "kv_hit" -> expect > 0.65 after priming

Staged shift plan (recommended): 10% -> 25% (30m) -> 50% (1h) -> 100% (2h), with automated rollback on 5xx > 3% over a 5m window or median latency > 2x baseline for 10m.

Known caveats: initial tokenization jitter on very long prompts can cause short tail latency spikes during warmup, and parallelized KV warming can temporarily raise CPU if priming concurrently at high concurrency. We include a soft-rate limit during priming to avoid amplification.

I've attached the liveness probe commands (text) and a trimmed kv_cache_warmup_log sample from our staging run. Marcus will call out the exact orchestration steps below.

Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: liveness_probe_commands.txt (text/plain, 2KB); kv_cache_warmup_log.txt (text/plain, 18KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Eric Lowry <eric.lowry@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gatecheck request — final week before VPC cutover

Adding technical specifics and runbook snippets. I'm writing this as the SRE/infra checklist we'll run during the activation window. Please paste these into your ticketing runbook if helpful.

Activation steps (chronological):
- 00:00 Pre-checks: confirm v4 routing table, internal LB health, KMS ACLs for the model key. Run ./scripts/check-preflight.sh -> exit 0.
- +05min: Enable read-only traffic to canary pool (10%). Monitor token counters via /metrics/token_stream_total and per-model 95p latency.
- +20min: Kick KV priming job (we'll push priming via our controller) with concurrency=8, batch_size=64. Expect ~18 minutes to reach 70% hit rate for the 50-top prefixes. See kv_cache_warmup_log.txt for sample.
- +45min: Validate probe responses on three control endpoints (us-east-1 private jump):
    * /health/liveness -> 200 within 200ms
    * /health/ready -> {ready:true, kv_state: warm}
    * /health/model_integrity -> checksums match deployed model
- +60 to +180min: ramp per staged plan; at each step run short verification load (3k tokens over 60s) to confirm latency and error budget.

Fallbacks: auto-switch to secondary model variant (smaller quantized) if 95p latency spikes > 2.5s. Manual rollback steps included in cutover_mop_v3.pdf.

I'll be on the bridge (Zoom link in Jira) and will push the priming job. If you want, we can remote into your jumpbox to run the acceptance curl tests with you.

—Marcus
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Eric Lowry <eric.lowry@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gatecheck request — final week before VPC cutover

Quick sign-off from product side and two minor asks before we lock the window:
1) Confirm SLA delta for the first 72h (we suggest a conservative 99.5% for the initial live tranche).
2) Please paste the exact observability tag keys we'll add to traces so Acme can map them to dashboards (we use trace.tag.service and trace.tag.deployment_id).

If both are OK I can sign the gate from Product and we can announce the go window to Support.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Eric Lowry <eric.lowry@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Gatecheck request — final week before VPC cutover

Laura — SLA delta confirmed: temporary 99.5% for first 72h. Observability tags: trace.tag.service="redwood-inference"; trace.tag.deployment_id="acme-vpc-20270610"; we will also emit metric labels: model_name, variant, kv_hit.

Final note: after a small staged warmup in staging today we hit 0.72 kv_hit after a 20-minute priming with concurrency=8; included ktail in kv_cache_warmup_log.txt. We'll be available on the bridge during the window and will run the acceptance curls from your jumpbox if you want remote pairing.

See you on Thu.

Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
